keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no row for the Tavastians. The page places them in 'the historical province of Tavastia (Häme)' with the core area round Lake Vanajavesi, hillforts in a line round Hämeenlinna and the largest hillfort in Finland at Rapola; no boundary or area. 1042 is the first dated mention. The modern regions Tavastia Proper, Päijät-Häme and Pirkanmaa are the researcher's reading of the province.

ledger.note: 1042: first mention, 'when Vladimir of Novgorod attacked them', the first time Finland appears in Russian texts. The page says Tavastia 'has been inhabited since the early Stone Age'; no founding is dated and no land changed hands, so the start is the first page-dated event, not a founding.

region.text: Tavastia (Häme): the modern regions Tavastia Proper, Päijät-Häme and Pirkanmaa, round Lake Vanajavesi, the core area on the page; the page gives no boundary

ledger.note: 1249: Tavastia passes to Sweden. 'The expedition has traditionally been dated to 1249-1250' and 'From 1249 onwards, sources generally regard' Tavastia as part of Sweden; the Swedes defeated the Tavastians 'under the leadership of Birger Jarl'. Some researchers argue for 1238-1239, so the year is carried at confidence 2. The castle the Swedes began building 'has traditionally been identified as Häme Castle' but may be Hakoinen; no founding year is given.

notes: Not a documented state: a tribal people (the page does not name a ruler, capital or institution). Start 1042 is the first page-dated event, not a founding. The Tavastians page is silent on the Swedish conquest date; the Second Swedish Crusade page gives the traditional 1249-1250 and the alternative 1238-1239. The page does not name Hämeenlinna as a capital or describe Tavastia as a Swedish province or county, so capitals is empty and the later Swedish administration of Häme is not drawn here. Cliopatria's Kingdom of Sweden shape for 1249-1250 should include Tavastia; this dossier is not a review of that shape.
